CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Implement the already-announced, dollar-matched retaliation on about $50 billion of US goods (soybeans, automobiles, aircraft) as soon as Washington publishes or activates the Section 301 list. Do not offer new purchase commitments or structural concessions while the tariff threat is live, and do not expand beyond that tit-for-tat package. Keep the Liu He channel open so that, if the US later suspends 301, the May framework of larger agricultural and energy purchases can be revived rather than discarded.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is material but not existential. USTR’s April 3 list targets aerospace, ICT, robotics and machinery—the Made in China 2025 stack—and the April 16 ZTE denial order showed the US can halt a national champion by cutting US components. The May 19 joint statement (China to “significantly increase” purchases; Mnuchin saying the trade war was “on hold”) collapsed on May 29 when the White House said it would proceed with 25% tariffs on ~$50B; Ross–Liu talks in early June produced no deal, and Beijing stated that all talk outcomes “will not take effect” if the US raises tariffs. Politico reporting through 12 June has the final list due around 15 June, with investment restrictions by 30 June. Against that, the real economy is not yet biting: China industrial production is still about +6% YoY, SA merchandise exports are still rising into June, CPI is soft, the discount rate is unchanged at 2.9%, and reserves remain ~$3.13T. CNY eased from April strength toward ~6.39 as the dollar firmed—pressure, not a 2015-style break. That mix sits between neutral and the +0.5 anchor (major export sectors hit / firm-level targeting), hence +0.38. Action should be mirror, not maximal: US G-7 isolation and farm-belt exposure (>$12B soy to China) give leverage if China stays proportionate; going beyond the April 4 list could invite the extra $100B Trump already floated in April; conceding purchases after the May walk-back would reward a collapsed truce. The 7 June ZTE settlement ($1B fine, escrow, board change) removes the most acute non-tariff fire without requiring China to pay on 301.
key_factors: Imminent Section 301 25% list on ~$50B targeting MIC 2025 sectors (aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery)
May 19 purchase-truce collapsed on May 29; Ross-Liu June talks failed; China conditioned all outcomes on no US tariffs
ZTE denial order demonstrated US component chokepoint; June 7 settlement eases that fire at a high political price
China macro still resilient: IP ~+6% YoY, exports still rising, reserves ~$3.13T, only mild CNY softening
Proportionate soy/auto/aircraft retaliation pressures US farm/industrial constituencies without inviting a $100B second wave

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
China industrial production still ~106.0 (same period previous year = 100) as of 2018-06; growth slowing modestly, not collapsing.
China SA merchandise exports still rising into June 2018 (~$211.6B) versus January (~$195.2B); tariffs not yet visible in export volumes.
China reserves excluding gold ~$3.13T in June 2018, down only ~1.5% over the window — no FX-stability crisis.
CNY ~6.3944 per USD on 2018-06-13; off April strength but far from a disorderly break.
China: "All economic and trade outcomes of the talks will not take effect if the U.S. side imposes any trade sanctions including raising tariffs."
Trump expected to impose tariffs as soon as Friday or next week; final list planned around 15 June; investment restrictions and export controls by 30 June.
Commerce announced a ZTE deal: $1B fine, $400M escrow, US compliance team, board and executive changes — lifting the denial order.
